subject: Android Programming
text: What does an Android Activity commonly represent?
optionA: A single screen or focused interaction in an application
explanation: An Activity is an application component that commonly represents a screen with which the user interacts.

subject: Android Programming
text: Which Activity lifecycle callback is called when an Activity is first created?
explanation: The system calls onCreate() when it creates the Activity; it is commonly used for initial setup and view creation.

subject: Android Programming
text: What is a common use of an explicit Intent in Android?
optionA: To start a specific application component by naming its class
optionB: To increase the device CPU clock
explanation: An explicit Intent identifies a target component, such as a particular Activity, that the application wants to start.

subject: Android Programming
text: Where are application components and many app-level permissions declared?
explanation: The Android manifest describes the application and declares components, required features and permissions as applicable.

subject: Android Programming
text: What is a key benefit of RecyclerView for displaying a scrolling list?
optionA: It requires every row to remain permanently attached to the screen
optionB: It reuses item views to efficiently display large or changing data sets
optionC: It stores all list items in the manifest
explanation: RecyclerView recycles item views as they move off screen, reducing unnecessary view creation and improving list performance.

subject: Android Programming
text: What is Android Room commonly used for?
optionA: A local persistence library that provides an abstraction layer over SQLite
optionB: A replacement for the Android package manager
optionD: A tool for drawing vector icons
explanation: Room is an Android persistence library built over SQLite that provides entities, DAOs and compile-time query checks.
